title: The Role of TP 43 and RNA in Auto-phagy
description: This segment discusses the involvement of specific proteins, such as TP 43, in the process of auto-phagy and its connection to RNA function in the brain. It highlights how TP 43 interacts with and regulates RNA processing, stability, and translation.
summary: The discussion focuses on the role of TP 43 in auto-phagy, which is identified as a major current cause of this process. TP 43 is presented as a central component, binding to over 6,000 targets. Furthermore, the text emphasizes the crucial interaction between TP 43 and RNA, noting that while RNA accounts for only about 30% of the total transcriptome in the brain, TP 43 plays a critical role in regulating RNA functions, including their splicing, transport, maturity, stability, and local translation.

title: Developing a Novel CRISPR-Based System for Single-Molecule RNA Visualization
description: This discussion outlines the development of a novel system combining fluorescent techniques and modified CRISPR-Cas9 to visualize and precisely localize specific RNA species within cells. The proposed system uses a modified Cas9 fused to a fluorescent protein, designed to target RNA with high specificity.
summary: The project aims to develop a technique for visualizing RNA in vivo with single-molecule precision, potentially utilizing C2 experiments and fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) combined with immunochemistry. This leads to the proposal of a modified CRISPR-Cas9 system for RNA targeting. The standard Cas9 system is replaced by a "dead" Cas9 (dCas9) fused to a fluorescent protein (GFP). This dCas9 is designed to localize in the nucleus via a specific signal (Tiger) when it is not forming the functional complex. The full system utilizes a modified single guide RNA (gRNA) and a pan-moter integrated into an oligo. This modification is intended to enhance the stability of the complex and improve the specificity required for targeting specific RNA species.

title: Live Imaging of RNA Dynamics for Genetic Forms in Zebrafish
description: This talk introduces the use of live imaging techniques to study RNA dynamics and genetic modifications in zebrafish. The speaker highlights why zebrafish are an ideal model system and proposes specific genetic tools for visualizing endogenous RNA localization within targeted cell populations.
summary: The speaker introduces their research focus on Live Imaging of RNA dynamics for genetic forms

title: The Central Role of RNA Binding Proteins in Disease: Understanding TDP-43 Interactions
description: This segment discusses the central role of TDP-43 and RNA binding proteins in maintaining protein and RNA homeostasis, and how their interaction with specific transcripts drives disease progression. It highlights the need for precise methods to study these complex interactions in pathological states.
summary: The speaker emphasizes the critical role of TDP-43 and other RNA binding proteins (like Sequestosome 1) in regulating protein and RNA homeostasis. They propose that these interactions are key drivers in disease progression through a feedforward loop that alters both protein and RNA homeostasis. Experimental evidence, including knockdown of Sequestosome 1 and co-injection of wild-type human TDP-43 mRNA, suggests a functional relationship between TDP-43 and Sequestosome 1, pointing to activity at the transcriptional level. The speaker concludes by stressing the urgent need for precise techniques—such as those allowing for localization and colocalization of RNA and protein components, and *in vivo* methods to quantify the dynamics and transport of these interactions—to fully understand the function of RNA binding proteins in pathology. The current model, combining genetic and imaging tools, is effective in establishing these interactions and provides a foundation for future research.
